findings.reason: The protected source is already expert-level interview code. `scores` directly expresses the only persistent state, `get(..., 0) + score` implements accumulation without branching, `nlargest` makes partial leader selection recognizable, and `del` relies on the source guarantee that reset targets an active player. The adapter replays the stateful interface without obscuring the native class. No candidate would materially improve correctness, asymptotic complexity, clarity, naming, or contract fidelity.

The score map contains exactly one accumulated total for each active player: `addScore` establishes or increases that total, and `reset` removes it so a later addition starts fresh. `nlargest(K, scores.values())` returns exactly the K greatest active totals, including distinct players with equal scores, and their sum is therefore the required query result. `top` does not mutate the map, so repeated queries observe identical state.

Expected hash-map access gives expected O(1) `addScore` and `reset`. With p active players, `top(K)` examines all p totals and performs heap-based partial selection in O(p log K) time under the manifest convention; the K = 1 specialization is linear, and selecting every player may use sorting while remaining within O(p log p). Persistent scores and temporary selection storage are bounded by O(p).

An independent dictionary-and-full-sort oracle computed every query from the current state. Oracle, protected app source, immutable native class, an independently written explicit size-K min-heap implementation, and the correct repeated-linear-maximum control agreed on all nine ordinary cases, all three benchmark tiers, and 5,000 deterministic schema-valid traces generated with seed 1244. App-local execution also preserved every operation trace.

The seeded traces exercised 137,479 additions, 56,975 repeated additions, 58,932 top queries, 40,589 resets, 20,476 reset-then-readd events, 19,605 top-one queries, 19,686 top-all queries, 6,874 queries over tied totals, 38,185 accumulated totals above the per-call score bound, and both player-ID and score bounds. A separate legal trace exercised the maximum 1,000 calls.

The partly hidden seven-row suite was replaced by nine explicit visible samples and trials. The exact source trace and output are preserved, while added rows expose cumulative scoring, tied leaders and a tie at the cutoff, top-one and top-all, repeated read-only queries, ranking changes across multiple K values, multiple resets, reset then re-add, player IDs 1 and 10000, added scores 1 and 100, and an accumulated total above 100.

The unchanged hidden tiers use 16, 64, and 256 active players with K equal to half the player count, legal deterministic scores, and exact oracle-derived outputs. Protected and the independent heap implementation passed the full scaling verdict in three runs each. The conventional O(Kp) repeated-linear-maximum control preserved all twelve outputs but failed only the scaling verdict in all three runs, with no timeout, safety-cap, or correctness failure.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode design problem 1244, Python as the primary language, and native entrypoint `Leaderboard`. Fresh authenticated evidence confirms an initially empty object, cumulative `addScore`, sum-of-top-K `top`, removal by `reset`, the active-player guarantees for K and reset, score increments from 1 through 100, player IDs through 10000, and at most 1000 calls.

The immutable native source remains bound to verified submission 2067989361 and is unchanged. Protected and native sources share the same `Leaderboard` class, score map, accumulation expression, `nlargest` query, deletion behavior, and asymptotic costs; the protected file adds only typing, documentation, and the required app-local operation-trace adapter.

The Approach was reviewed against both protected implementations. Its three required sections accurately derive map state, partial top-K selection, tie behavior, reset semantics, app trace replay, expected update costs, query and space bounds, and the tradeoffs of sorting, repeated selection, ordered storage, and score buckets. Its edge cases cover every material state transition without leaking an alternative contract.

The modular Reference preserves the initially empty state, all three operations and their exact semantics, the native and app-local contracts, the single source command trace and output, every intermediate explanation step, all four constraints, and all three source hints. The authenticated statement contains no images, diagrams, tables, note, or follow-up section.

A fresh authenticated Premium review confirmed one explained example, four constraints, three hints, and no source visuals or tables. `source_fidelity.json` binds all five modular Reference files to live statement hash 2ebccd4e0201b2af6a149fff0932264da622090cbd3255be5dfb0d0abcd5847e and validates without errors.
